{
  "research_question": "Do stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) differentially affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Time-to-Target: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. Continuous, approximately normal (though max=201.4 suggests right skew), variance check needed. If variance heterogeneity severe, consider Welch's ANOVA.",
    "Success: Binary outcome (0/1). Standard ANOVA inappropriate. Use logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as categorical predictor, or chi-square test of independence, or generalized linear model with binomial family. Report odds ratios relative to reference paradigm (e.g., Sham).",
    "Path Efficiency: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. Highly right-skewed (max=29.8 vs mean=0.47). Log-transformation or non-parametric alternative (Kruskal-Wallis) likely needed.",
    "Average Speed: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. Check normality and homogeneity of variance. Right tail present (max=75.4) but less extreme than Path Efficiency.",
    "AD (Angular Dispersion): One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. Bounded [0,1], mean=0.38, sd=0.24. Beta regression or arcsine transformation may improve model fit, but standard ANOVA may be acceptable if diagnostics pass."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: Assumed from experimental design; verify no temporal autocorrelation within mice (residual plots by Mouse).",
    "Normality: Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests on residuals for each continuous variable. Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, and Average Speed show right skew; log-transformation may be required.",
    "Homogeneity of variance: Levene's test or Brown-Forsythe test. Given unequal group sizes (Combined n=48846 vs Sham n=3505), variance heterogeneity is a major concern.",
    "Sample size: Extremely unbalanced (Combined ~14x larger than Sham). Robust methods or permutation ANOVA recommended for valid inference.",
    "Outliers: Examine standardized residuals; Path Efficiency max=29.8 is extreme relative to mean=0.47 and warrants investigation."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If omnibus ANOVA significant for Time-to-Target: Games-Howell post-hoc tests (unequal variances and sample sizes) or Tukey-Kramer with Welch correction. Focus on Sham vs. active stimulation paradigms.",
    "If omnibus test significant for Path Efficiency (after transformation or using Kruskal-Wallis): Dunn's test with Bonferroni or FDR correction for pairwise comparisons.",
    "If omnibus test significant for Average Speed: Same as Time-to-Target (Games-Howell or Tukey-Kramer).",
    "If omnibus test significant for AD: Same as Time-to-Target; consider whether bounded nature requires specialized post-hoc for beta regression.",
    "For Success (logistic regression): Wald tests for pairwise contrasts with multiple comparison correction, or estimated marginal means with Tukey adjustment on log-odds scale."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Sham paradigm expected to show poorest performance: lowest Success (0.273), highest Time-to-Target (4.68s), lowest Path Efficiency (0.308), lowest Average Speed (10.74), and lowest AD (0.236).",
    "Combined stimulation expected to show best or near-best performance: high Success (0.780), low Time-to-Target (2.56s), high Path Efficiency (0.502), high Average Speed (12.83), high AD (0.399).",
    "Bright Visual Only expected to outperform Dim Visual Only: Success 0.785 vs 0.673, Time-to-Target 2.61s vs 3.14s, Path Efficiency 0.504 vs 0.434, AD 0.387 vs 0.336.",
    "ICMS Only and Dim Visual Only expected to show intermediate performance, similar to each other but below Combined and Bright Visual Only.",
    "AD pattern suggests more directed movement (lower angular dispersion) with less effective stimulation, consistent with straighter paths in better-performing conditions."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe imbalance in group sizes (Combined n=48846, Sham n=3505) reduces power for Sham comparisons and inflates Type I error risk with standard ANOVA.",
    "Success is binary: ANOVA assumptions fundamentally violated; logistic regression required but interpretation differs.",
    "Path Efficiency extreme right skew (max/mean ratio ~63) suggests outliers or data quality issues; transformation or robust methods essential.",
    "Single-factor analysis ignores Mouse as random effect; 8 mice with repeated measures structure not accounted for in simple ANOVA.",
    "No information on trial-level temporal structure or learning effects across sessions.",
    "Temperature=0.0 in metadata suggests deterministic LLM output; no uncertainty quantification from model sampling."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit mixed-effects models with Mouse as random intercept for each continuous response variable, using Stim Paradigm as fixed effect. For Success, use generalized linear mixed model (GLMM) with binomial family. Apply log-transformation to Path Efficiency and possibly Time-to-Target. Report estimated marginal means with 95% confidence intervals and pairwise comparisons with Tukey or Games-Howell adjustment. Conduct sensitivity analyses excluding extreme Path Efficiency outliers (>3 SD or >10)."
}
